name: Immunodeficiency Syndrome with Autoimmunity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Criteria for Immunodeficiency Syndrome with Autoimmunity

criteria.description: Presence of one or more autoimmune diseases confirmed by clinical and laboratory findings
Documented immunodeficiency characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia or impaired lymphocyte function
Exclusion of secondary causes of immunodeficiency and autoimmunity such as infections or malignancies
Positive family history of immunodeficiency or autoimmune disorders
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with combined immunodeficiency and autoimmunity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both autoimmune manifestations and documented immunodeficiency with exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including immunology and rheumatology assessments.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent bacterial infections with autoimmune cytopenias
pathognomonic.notes: Combination of infections and autoimmune blood disorders is highly indicative
searchTerms: repeated bacterial infections with low blood cell counts
bacterial infections plus autoimmune blood disorders
immune system destroying red blood cells
red blood cell breakdown from antibodies
ongoing chest and sinus bacterial infections

common.symptomName: Chronic diarrhea due to autoimmune enteropathy
searchTerms: chronic diarrhea from immune gut disease
persistent diarrhea due to gut immune attack
inflamed joints due to immune system

occasional.symptomName: Oral ulcers related to autoimmune mucositis
searchTerms: painful oral ulcers due to immune attack

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary fibrosis secondary to autoimmune inflammation
searchTerms: chronic lung damage due to immune disease

laboratory: Low serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Positive autoantibodies (e.g., ANA, anti-dsDNA, anti-platelet antibodies)
imaging: Chest CT showing bronchiectasis or chronic lung changes
Abdominal ultrasound revealing splenomegaly or lymphadenopathy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as CTLA4, LRBA, STAT3, or other immune regulatory genes
other: Histopathology of affected tissues showing lymphocytic infiltration and autoimmune damage

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly immunodeficiency without prominent autoimmune cytopenias
Later onset in adolescence or adulthood

redFlags: Severe recurrent infections despite standard treatment
Failure to thrive or growth retardation in pediatric patients
references: Orange JS, et al. Immunodeficiency with Autoimmunity: Clinical and Molecular Features. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2023.
Orphanet Report on Immunodeficiency Syndrome with Autoimmunity, ORPHA:169355.
